sources_opened.version: Rick Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, Version 5, January 11, 2019 (author PDF; title page checked); matches handbook/bib/handbook.bib key DurrettPTEAuthor2019 and the held-sources record
sources_opened.pages: printed pp. 52-56 (sec. 2.1.4 including thm. 2.1.21 p. 53, the nice-space definition and remarks p. 53, thm. 2.1.22 with proof and caveat p. 54; PDF pp. 60-64); pp. 462-467 (app. A.3 on pp. 464-466 in full; PDF pp. 470-475)

components.source_items_compared: Durrett p. 53 (R^N as all real sequences, coordinates X_i, product sigma-field generated by the finite dimensional sets {omega_i in B_i, 1 <= i <= n}) and app. A.3, p. 464 (generation by the finite dimensional rectangles with -inf <= a_i < b_i <= inf). The p. 53 generating class is the coordinate product sigma-algebra of thm:p15-coded-space-extension with real factors; see defect_observations.
Durrett Theorem 2.1.21, p. 53 and Theorem A.3.1, p. 464 (consistency on rectangles with a whole-line last coordinate); no independence assumed.

Durrett app. A.3, pp. 464-465 (S is a semialgebra; the algebra of finite disjoint unions; the finite-union case of additivity). Semialgebra, both algebras, generated sigma-algebras, extension of consistency to Borel sets, well-definedness and finite additivity of p_0 are proved.
Durrett app. A.3, p. 465 (compact rectangles used in the approximation).

Durrett app. A.3, p. 465 (C_n inside B_n, a finite union of closed bounded rectangles with P(B_n - C_n) <= delta/2^(n+1)). Compactness of closed boxes, tightness and the inner approximation are proved.

Durrett Lemma A.3.3, pp. 465-466 (B_n in A decreasing to the empty set gives P(B_n) to 0; compact approximation and diagonal argument; the source's strategy remark). Every step is written with indices specified.

Durrett Theorem 2.1.21, p. 53 and Theorem A.3.1 with its proof, pp. 464-465 (existence and uniqueness of P on (R^N, R^N) with the rectangle values (*)). Proved through countable additivity on the algebra and the proved premeasure-extension theorem; uniqueness, coordinate measurability and finite-dimensional laws written.

Durrett p. 53 (finite construction P = mu_1 x ... x mu_n and the aim of an infinite independent sequence with given distribution functions) and Example A.3.2, p. 464 (product rectangle masses; coordinates independent with distributions F_n). Proved, with the dyadic identification.

Durrett p. 53 (nice: one-to-one map into R with the map and its inverse measurable, no Borel-image clause; the remark that such spaces are often called standard Borel spaces and the stated reason for not using the name; adequacy for later results). The source definition, its exact relation to Borel real codings and the naming remark are stated and proved on the route.
Durrett p. 54 (binary expansion with infinitely many 0's; the interleaving .x^1_1 x^1_2 x^2_1 x^1_3 x^2_2 x^3_1 ...). theta(j,k) reproduces the printed order (checked for the first eight positions).
Durrett p. 54 (special case S = [0,1)^N with rho(x,y) = sum |x_n - y_n|/2^n and the map phi_o). Metric and product sigma-algebras, the Borel image E_0 and the measurable inverse are proved.

Durrett Theorem 2.1.22 and its proof, p. 54 (d = rho/(1+rho); dense q_1, q_2, ... in S; psi continuous and one-to-one; phi_o o psi) with the caveat that the proof is light on details. Completed construction and the statement in the source's own terms (three readings of the Borel sets of S) are proved.

Durrett p. 53 (need for sequences in other measurable spaces; Theorem 2.1.21 not valid for arbitrary measurable spaces, first example by Andersen and Jessen (1948) on a product of different spaces, with Halmos (1950) p. 214 and Neveu (1965) p. 84, and Wegner (1973) for identical factors; the claim that the generalization to nice spaces is trivial). Failure claim and attributions reported as the source names them; the nice-space generalization is settled (uniqueness always, existence with Borel images, failure without) with proofs.
No counterpart example on pp. 53-54 or in app. A.3; the inconsistent pair and the null infinite fair-bit event are argued at the cited lines.

Durrett p. 54 (Caveat emptor; Section 13.1 of Dudley (1989); the consequence that Borel subsets of a complete separable metric space are finite, countably infinite or of the cardinality of the reals, phrased by the source as the continuum hypothesis holding for them). The boundary is accurate and the cardinality statement is proved on the route with its source framing.

defect_observations: C015: the boundary still says the cardinality statement needs a separate perfect-set argument and does not point to sec:p15-w02c-p15-004-borel-cardinality, where it is now proved (that section points back). A forward cross-reference belongs in this read-only host (lead-owned edit).

C013 annex lines 462-465: identifying the product sigma-algebra on E^(n) with the trace Borel sigma-algebra uses the fact that traces of generators generate the trace sigma-algebra; the fact is proved later on the route (thm:p15-w02c-p15-003-trace-generation, handbook/parts/p15/measure-integration-and-product-constructions-w02c-p15-003.tex line 331) but is not cited here.
C003 annex line 35 asserts that half-open rectangles are Borel without an argument; the argument is on the route in annex:p15-w02c-p15-014-rectangles part (2).

C001: Durrett's p. 53 generating class {omega_i in B_i, 1 <= i <= n}, B_i Borel, is not named in the countable chapter; it generates the coordinate product sigma-algebra used in thm:p15-coded-space-extension and thm:p15-w02c-p15-004-nice-extension, and lies between the rectangular cylinders S and the Borel cylinders C, so its equality with F_infinity follows from thm:p15-cylinder-consistency in one step that is not written out.
